observations.trace: GpuBody::new checks nonempty vertex count, matching normal/UV/skin-array lengths, joint-count equality and face index bounds, before uploading raw body data and converting counts to u32. DeviceBreastplate records morph position/normal buffers without names and later zips recorded slots with a separate names slice; each mapped mesh checks its normal status in read_mesh. With two recorded morphs and one name, the second pair and its per-mesh status are omitted by that zip after shared status/readback. The selected character-creator caller loops over input.morphs to record, then collects names from the same ordered input before read.
observations.remaining: Conditional source control-flow only; no body, GPU, staged read, morph or export ran. Selected caller does not demonstrate mismatch; other callers and readback failures remain open. Original Adler344 explicitly extended q137 to breastplate, so preserve one connected family and both source owners.

observations.trace: GpuBody::new checks structural lengths, indices and joint-count alignment but does not inspect component finiteness or normalize the f32 positions, normals, UVs or weights before issuing uploads. The selected public character-creator bracer path first checks domain and structural agreement and then passes body arrays to GpuBody::new; its shown input validator also does not perform finite checks. Assuming all structural and rig-family requirements hold, a position containing NaN reaches the upload call in source control flow.
observations.remaining: No input, float operation, upload, kernel, output or test ran. Actual producer constraints and downstream GPU/status checks remain open; no malformed published mesh is asserted. This is related to historical skin-weight q167/q175, not established as the same contract or alias.

observations.contract: Coordinate field revision and fitted garment boundaries
observations.trace: Original coord2183 had Normal, AngleWeightedNormal and Radial extrusion and a geometric kernel. Current adds FieldNormal and FieldAngleWeightedNormal, a kernel field capability, per-carrier tagged kind/direction writes, and a check rejecting field shell extrusion with a geometric-only kernel. PartBuild reserves five words per carrier; the shell kernel reads fitted directions for field modes and flags invalid/nonfinite/zero vectors or unknown tags. Selected body cloth uses a field-capable kernel and FieldNormal; selected skirt uses a field-capable kernel and chooses field weighting, and its source explicitly retains geometric extrusion for free or mixed points.
observations.remaining: Source and WGSL inspection only: no shader compilation, validation, dispatch or fit ran. Allocation arithmetic, all stage-order dependencies, actual shader outputs and other consumers remain open. The selected mixed-field geometric path is documented behavior, not automatically a fallback defect.

observations.contract: Body-cloth integer ordinal encoded in f32
observations.trace: record_body_cloth accepts public u32 layer point_count, validates local index bounds and finite positive geometry parameters, then forms coordinates with each global point ordinal as f32. Both body-cloth vertex and fitted-extrusion shader sources cast coord.x back to u32 to address the fitted point table. In binary32, the integer 16777217 is halfway between representable 16777216 and16777218; Rust integer-to-float casts use ties-to-even, so this ordinal rounds to16777216. If a point table and the accumulated layers reach that ordinal and all necessary allocation/device limits permit recording, it addresses the preceding point rather than preserving its identity.
observations.remaining: No large layer, cast, allocation, GPU, shader or output ran; this is exact source/spec reasoning conditional on a very large input. Real source mesh limits, prior layer accumulation, device buffers and whether such inputs are supported remain open; separate u32 accumulation overflow is also unassessed. No claim that ordinary garments are affected.
